what_happened: While a drain (budget 25, job limit 10) was running through its queue oldest first, the owner asked for a newer request (the CI-compute one) to go ahead of 20 older queued items. The drain has no priority setting and no graceful stop. The operator killed the drain process, which interrupted job g61b mid-run, so the new request could go first.
cause: The drain was built as a plain oldest-first consumer. Queue items carry no priority and the drain has no control channel to stop after the current job or to reorder pending items. The only lever an operator has over a running drain is killing the process, and that cuts a job off mid-run. Reprioritising is a normal owner action, so the design should have allowed for it.
prevention: Add a priority field to queue items, with the drain picking the highest priority first and the oldest within a priority. Re-read the queue between jobs so a newly added urgent item is picked up at the next job boundary. Add a graceful stop (for example `athena drain --stop`, or a stop file) that lets the current job finish and then exits. Make an interrupted job resumable or retryable, so a forced kill never strands it. Log any manual kill as an intervention.
proposed_request: Make the athena drain respect priority and stop gracefully. Outcome: the owner can put a newer request ahead of older queued items, and can pause the drain, without killing a running job. Requirements: (1) queue items have a priority (default normal), and an operator command can raise one; (2) the drain picks the highest priority first and the oldest first within a priority, re-reading the queue before each job so an item added or raised mid-drain runs next; (3) a graceful stop command makes a running drain finish its current job and exit, and reports what remains; (4) if a job is interrupted anyway, it is marked retryable and not left stuck. Acceptance: tests show that an item raised while a drain runs is taken at the next job boundary, ahead of 20 older normal-priority items; that the stop command lets the current job complete before the drain exits; and that a killed drain leaves its job retryable.
